paper_title: Improved constraints on non-Newtonian forces at 10 microns
notes: Non-Newtonian gravity (Yukawa) fifth-force test with a cryogenic micro-cantilever. Headline result is the 95% CL exclusion on |alpha| (Yukawa strength relative to Newtonian gravity, V = -G m1 m2/r (1 + alpha exp(-r/lambda))) versus range lambda, from Table V (also plotted as 'Stanford 3' in Fig. 9). Values (lambda[um], alpha): (4, 3.1e7), (6, 4.6e5), (10, 1.4e4), (18, 1.1e3), (34, 2.5e2), (66, 1.5e2). Best bound |alpha|>14000 at lambda=10 um. Range lambda converted to mediator mass via m = 1.97e-7 eV*m / lambda_m (task-card ScalarNucleon fifth-force rule); e.g. lambda=10 um -> m=1.97e-2 eV. Reported in native alpha (Yukawa strength) variable since the paper does not provide a scalar-nucleon coupling g_N. Limit does not depend on dark-matter density.
